# SNP Manifesto 2015 Summary: Stronger for Scotland

The Scottish National Party's 2015 manifesto presents a vision of Scotland gaining greater influence at Westminster to deliver progressive change, protect public services, and challenge the "out of touch Westminster system."

## Core Message
Leader Nicola Sturgeon pledges that SNP MPs will "always stand up for Scotland's best interests" and make Scotland's voice heard "more loudly than it has ever been heard before." The SNP positions itself as the only party that can force genuine progressive change, arguing that Labour alone won't be bold enough to deliver what ordinary people need.

## Economic Approach
The manifesto firmly rejects austerity, proposing instead "responsible increases in public spending" and investment in infrastructure to create jobs. The SNP criticizes the Conservative-Liberal Democrat approach as fundamentally flawed, noting borrowing has risen substantially despite stated targets. They propose releasing over £140 billion in additional public expenditure over the next parliament compared to existing government plans.

Key economic proposals include increasing the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020, establishing a Scottish Business Development Bank, reducing Air Passenger Duty to boost tourism, and seeking additional investment in infrastructure including high-speed rail connecting Scotland to England.

## Social Justice
The manifesto prioritizes fairness and tackling inequality. Immediate priorities include abolishing the Bedroom Tax, halting the rollout of Universal Credit and Personal Independence Payments, and increasing Carer's Allowance. The SNP supports higher taxes on the wealthy, including restoring the 50p top tax rate and introducing a mansion tax.

## Public Services
Healthcare receives prominent focus, with proposals for £2 billion additional NHS funding by 2020-21 and opposition to privatization. Education commitments include maintaining free university tuition, expanding Modern Apprenticeships to 30,000 annually, and nearly doubling free childcare provision.

## Defence and Nuclear Weapons
The SNP maintains principled opposition to Trident renewal, arguing the £100 billion cost over 35 years should instead fund health and education. They support conventional defence spending while seeking greater military investment in Scotland.

## Further Devolution
While supporting independence, the manifesto acknowledges "that is not what this election is about." Instead, the SNP demands the Smith Commission proposals be delivered in full while pushing for additional powers over employment, welfare, and taxation—arguing current proposals leave over 70% of Scottish taxes and 85% of welfare spending at Westminster, insufficient for tackling inequality.

## Political Positioning
The manifesto explicitly states the SNP will "never put the Tories into power" and will work with other parties to "lock the Tories out" if an anti-Tory majority exists. This frames the election as a choice between continued Westminster austerity and a fairer, more progressive alternative championed by Scotland.
